Title: Diagnosis of test `testExactOptionNameMatch`

Details: The test method `testExactOptionNameMatch` invokes the parsing of command-line options by calling `new DefaultParser().parse(getOptions(), new String[]{"--prefix"});` where `getOptions()` returns two options with long names `"prefix"` and `"prefixplusplus"`.

From the code of `DefaultParser.parse`, parsing eventually calls `handleToken` for each argument. For an argument starting with "--", it calls `handleLongOption`. Since the argument in the test is `"--prefix"` (without "="), `handleLongOptionWithoutEqual` is called.

Inside `handleLongOptionWithoutEqual`, options that match the token are retrieved via `options.getMatchingOptions(token)`. If no matches are found, `handleUnknownToken` is called. If multiple matches are found, an `AmbiguousOptionException` is thrown.

Because the test failed, it suggests that the parser is throwing an ambiguity exception rather than accepting `"--prefix"` as a valid option. Most likely, this is because the token `"--prefix"` matches both options `"prefix"` and `"prefixplusplus"`, causing multiple matches and ambiguity.

The root cause is that the matching logic in `getMatchingOptions` is allowing prefix matches rather than enforcing an exact match of the long option name when parsing long options without an equals sign.

Hence, the test failure points to the method that finds matching options by partial prefix matching, which results in ambiguity when a shorter option matches the prefix of a longer option.

The fix should ensure that exact long option name matches are prioritized or only exact matches are considered for options specified without trailing "=".

Recommended locations to fix:

org.apache.commons.cli.Options.getMatchingOptions(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.cli.DefaultParser.handleLongOptionWithoutEqual(java.lang.String)

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
